title: Magic

description.main: KangHee Kim's first photobook, Magic, collects the Photoshop collages of her Street Errands project, in which New York street scenes are spliced with clouds, skies and distant landscapes into small moments that could not have happened. Same Paper, Shanghai, autumn 2016, first edition of 400.
description.extended:
KangHee Kim's first photobook, Magic, collects the Photoshop collages of her Street Errands project, in which New York street scenes are spliced with clouds, skies and distant landscapes into small moments that could not have happened.

The series began in 2016 on errands around the city, when Kim stopped waiting for something remarkable to occur and started building it from her own archive of snapshots. She works against the commercial use of the software, which hides every seam; here the joins are left showing, and the pleasure is in the fit of two pictures that were never meant to meet. Same Paper of Shanghai published the book in autumn 2016 as a thread-sewn hardcover of 60 pages, 15.5 × 21.4 cm, in a first edition of 400 copies, designed by Jinkui Zhou. The cover photograph, a low cloud sitting on a two-lane road, carries the title in green foil set on a slant.

Kim, born in Seoul, studied painting at the Maryland Institute College of Art and lives in New York. Her visa status has kept her from travelling outside the United States, and she has described the collages as a way of making the trips she cannot take. Same Paper followed Magic with Golden Hour in 2018, and Setanta Books published Dreamer, a larger survey of the same project, in 2022.
description.artist_bio: KangHee Kim, born in Seoul, lives and works in New York. She studied painting at the Maryland Institute College of Art and came to photography in her final year. Her books are Magic (Same Paper, 2016), Golden Hour (Same Paper, 2018) and Dreamer (Setanta Books, 2022).
